claims.text: Equal-atomic NbMoTaW has a homogeneous single-phase BCC structure in its untreated state.
Untreated NbMoTaW exhibits poor room-temperature ductility.
NbMoTaW has excellent high-temperature mechanical performance, including at 1600 °C.
A controlled thermo-mechanical treatment can induce an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure in NbMoTaW.
A minor Al addition can promote B2 formation in NbMoTaW.
The targeted inverted microstructure consists of a continuous BCC matrix containing dispersed discrete B2 precipitates.
Replacing a continuous B2 matrix with a continuous BCC matrix and discrete B2 precipitates improves room-temperature compressive ductility in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The continuous BCC matrix enhances room-temperature plastic deformation.
Discrete B2 precipitates disrupt crack propagation.
An inverted BCC+B2 microstructure can preserve elevated-temperature yield strength while improving room-temperature ductility.
Preserving the overall matrix composition and phase stability will prevent degradation of irradiation resistance.
Processed NbMoTaW will show a significant increase in room-temperature plastic strain before failure relative to untreated NbMoTaW.
Processed NbMoTaW will retain yield strength at 1600 °C comparable to untreated NbMoTaW.
Processed NbMoTaW will retain irradiation resistance comparable to untreated NbMoTaW.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix is associated with poor room-temperature ductility in two-phase refractory high-entropy alloys.
Excessive or continuous B2 formation could diminish high-temperature performance.
Excessive or continuous B2 formation could alter irradiation resistance.

The hypothesis is falsified if room-temperature ductility improves by less than 15%, or if high-temperature strength or irradiation resistance declines by more than 10% relative to untreated controls.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator consistently specifies a continuous BCC matrix, whereas the mechanism calls the BCC matrix 'discrete.'
The alloying branch of the intervention introduces Al and changes composition, while the irradiation rationale assumes that the overall matrix composition is preserved.

The initial material is single-phase BCC and the intervention deliberately creates a BCC+B2 state, yet the irradiation rationale states that phase stability is preserved without clarifying whether this means stability of the new two-phase microstructure rather than retention of the original phase state.
